input.quote: However, any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than one (1) year's prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties.
input.rationale: Paragraph 18 gives us no convenience exit during the twenty-five year Initial Period: 18.1 (p0228) allows a Party to terminate its participation only at the end of the Initial Period or thereafter on one year's notice, and 18.2 (p0229) permits mid-term termination only by unanimous written agreement of all Parties, with 18.5 (p0233) denying any capital-cost credit on exit. Absence of any customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory, so this fails fallback. The counterparty side is already compliant and better than the playbook asks (no mid-term unilateral exit for the other Parties; one year's notice at term end), so we left it untouched and inserted a single new Subparagraph 18.8 giving Teleglobe USA Inc. alone a convenience termination on thirty days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts. Because the new right sits outside Subparagraph 18.1, the no-capital-cost-credit rule in 18.5 and the continuing-liability tail in 18.7 are unaffected.

proposal.summary: Add a Teleglobe-only convenience exit on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a convenience exit for Teleglobe USA Inc. on thirty days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of amounts it has prepaid, since Paragraph 18 otherwise locks us in for the full twenty-five year Initial Period. The right is ours alone, so the other Parties remain unable to walk away mid-term.

ops.text: In addition to Subparagraph 18.1, Teleglobe USA Inc. may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time by giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Parties, and the other Parties shall refund to Teleglobe USA Inc., pro rata, any amounts prepaid by it for the period after the effective date of such termination.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
